assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window: the detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, built on a cubic-kilometre instrument in Antarctic ice. As an instrument builder I value that the detector concept was itself the decisive achievement. The science has since produced source associations (TXS 0506+056 blazar, NGC 1068, Galactic plane), turning a detector into a new astronomy.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the IceCube concept and its predecessor AMANDA, and Spiering was a central figure in the neutrino-telescope programme and its collaboration-building. Both supplied credited names are well supported. The collaboration is large and other leaders (including early Baikal, DUMAND and ANTARES pioneers and current spokespeople) have claims, but a two-person prize is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Strong. The diffuse flux was observed in 2013 and confirmed with independent channels and years of additional data; multi-messenger source evidence has accumulated over roughly a decade. Timely, with the field now producing results rather than just promises.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs Halzen and Spiering against other pioneers of neutrino telescopes (Baikal, DUMAND, AMANDA, ANTARES) is not settled by the supplied credit.
Source identification remains statistically modest for individual objects; the diffuse flux is the firm result.
I have not independently verified the details of the source associations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached fractional uncertainties at the 10^-18 level, opening a route to redefining the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The idea (magic-wavelength trapping) is original and the measurement is clean and quantitative, which appeals to an experimentalist.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock; Ye built the highest-performing systems and drove their precision and comparison. The two-name credit is coherent, although others (e.g. Pritchard-era trapping, Takamoto, Lemonde, Derevianko theory) have contributions I cannot fully weigh.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent laboratories reproduce and surpass the benchmarks, and international metrological work toward a redefinition of the second is under way. The 2005 prize (frequency combs) and 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) mean the area is adjacent to earlier awards but not duplicative.
uncertainties: Overlap with Ye's role in the thorium nuclear-clock candidate and with earlier clock prizes could be argued as cumulative.
Whether a redefinition of the second will have happened affects timing; I do not know its current status.
Possible need to credit theory (Derevianko, Katori's collaborators) is not resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first direct images of a black-hole shadow (M87*, then Sgr A*) are a landmark of precision measurement, combining VLBI at 1.3 mm, calibration and imaging methodology to test strong-field gravity. The impact on public and scientific awareness is large and the result is clear.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed imaging the shadow and led the scientific case; Doeleman led the global array and instrumentation effort; Zensus led the European VLBI community and the collaboration structure. The result was produced by a collaboration of hundreds, so any three-person prize is a simplification and the imaging-algorithm and calibration contributors are not credited.
assessment.maturity: The M87* image has been re-observed with consistent ring size, and Sgr A* was imaged independently, supporting robustness. The interpretation (GR-consistent shadow) is stable, though the constraints on alternatives remain limited. The 2020 prize for black-hole theory and the Galactic-centre orbits makes this a complementary rather than duplicative recognition.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration credit allocation is genuinely contested.
Imaging reconstruction choices and polarization interpretation remain under active study.
Whether the committee views the discovery as a technique/instrument achievement or an astrophysical discovery matters for how to frame the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting the flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and then demonstrating correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the field of moire quantum materials, with a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. The theory-experiment pairing is rare and clean.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental discovery. This trio matches the decisive contributions well, though Cory Dean, Pablo's collaborators and others (including Kim, Young) contributed to the broader moire field.
assessment.maturity: Several independent groups reproduced the correlated phases within a short time, and the field is very active. Some questions remain on the origin of the superconductivity and on sample-to-sample variability, so interpretation is still evolving; recognition would be timely rather than overdue.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity in the flat band is unresolved.
Broader moire-material discoveries (hBN-aligned systems, fractional Chern insulators, other TMD moire systems) may need to be framed together or separated.
Possible premature recognition relative to the stability of the interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Introduction of the Z2 topological classification and the quantum spin Hall insulator, followed by experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, created the field of topological insulators. The conceptual importance is high and the lasting influence on condensed-matter physics and materials discovery is clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 invariant in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed the edge conduction in HgTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied credit omits the BHZ theorists (Shoucheng Zhang, deceased; Bernevig, Hughes) and the three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Hsieh and Hasan), so attribution is incomplete and difficult.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: confirmed in many materials, with 3D topological insulators observed independently. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and phases, and the committee may view this as a natural follow-on.
uncertainties: Credit problems: Zhang's death and the Hasan/Fu/Moore contributions complicate a fair three-person configuration.
Relationship to the 2016 topological-phase prize may be seen as overlapping.
Mele's and Kane's graphene gap was later found to be tiny, so the experiment came from a different platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a foundational application of quantum mechanics, with an original protocol (BB84), an entanglement-based variant (E91) and proof of security that connects to Bell tests. It has been implemented in fibre and satellite links, giving real-world relevance.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84; Ekert proposed the entanglement-based protocol. This is a natural trio drawn from the credited names, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea (deceased) and security-proof contributors (Mayers, Lo-Chau, Shor-Preskill) are not credited.
assessment.maturity: The protocols are decades old and have been demonstrated across many platforms, including satellite QKD (Micius). The 2022 prize on entanglement experiments and Bell inequalities lies adjacent; the scientific significance is as much information theory as physics, and practical security of real devices remains debated.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as physics versus computer science or cryptography.
Overlap with the 2022 entanglement prize.
Unconditional versus device-level security is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed states of light beat the standard quantum limit and are now routinely used in gravitational-wave detectors, demonstrating a concrete payoff of quantum optics to a Nobel-recognised instrument. Caves proposed their use in interferometry; the experimental development is sustained. The lasting impact for precision measurement is clear.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the theoretical proposal for squeezed-light interferometry; Kimble led the first experimental squeezing demonstrations (with Slusher and others); Schnabel led the squeezed-light work toward GEO600-scale detectors. Mavalvala and many LIGO colleagues also contributed, and Slusher and Walls are significant omissions, so attribution is intricate.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is operating in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600 and has been independently implemented. Mature enough, with ongoing improvements, although the full recognition story is tied to gravitational-wave detection, already recognised in 2017.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2017 gravitational-wave prize and with the 2012 prize (Haroche, Wineland) on quantum control.
Exactly who should be in a trio is unclear given Slusher, Walls, Mavalvala and others.
Nature of the credit as an enabling technology rather than a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BeppoSAX X-ray afterglow localisation and the subsequent optical and radio redshift measurements settled the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts, one of the major astrophysical puzzles of the 20th century. As someone who works on GRB instrumentation and polarimetry I acknowledge familiarity with the field and treat that cautiously; the discovery is nevertheless clear and fundamental.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led BeppoSAX detection of the X-ray afterglow (GRB 970228); Kulkarni's group provided early optical and radio follow-up and the distance scale. Others, notably van Paradijs, Groot, Piro, Djorgovski, Metzger and Frail, also have strong claims, and some key people are deceased, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: afterglows are now routine, the cosmological origin is established, and the field includes Swift, Fermi and gravitational-wave-associated events. The long delay since 1997 raises the question of whether the window of timeliness has passed.
uncertainties: Substantial and disputed credit among BeppoSAX, optical and radio teams.
Given my own instrument background in gamma-ray astronomy, I should not weigh this in a self-serving way and rely on the evidence rather than familiarity.
I have not independently checked who is deceased among possible claimants.
